claims.label: Theorem 1
claims.statement_original:
In the regression model (13), consider the heavy-tailed series prior (3) with parameters specified by (5) and (7)–(8) as well as (14) with $q=2$. Suppose $f_0\in\mathcal S^\beta(L)$ for some $\beta,L>0$. Then, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
E_{f_0}\Pi\left[\{f:\|f-f_0\|_2>\mathcal L_nn^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\}\mid X^{(n)}\right]\to0,
\]
where $\mathcal L_n=(\log n)^d$ for some $d>0$. Further, the same result holds, with a possibly different $d$, for the choice of $(\sigma_k)$ as in (6), provided $\alpha\ge\beta$. Both results also hold for truncated priors at $k=n$, that are the same as the ones considered except they set $f_k=0$ for $k>n$.

claims.label: Theorem 2
claims.statement_original:
In the inverse regression model (15) with degree of ill–posedness of the forward operator $\nu\ge0$, consider the heavy-tailed series prior (3) with parameters specified by (5) and (7)–(8) as well as (14) with $q=2$. Suppose $f_0\in\mathcal S^\beta(L)$ for some $\beta,L>0$. Then, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
E_{f_0}\Pi[\{f:\|f-f_0\|_2>\mathcal L_nn^{-\beta/(2\beta+2\nu+1)}\}\mid X^{(n)}]\to0,
\]
where $\mathcal L_n=(\log n)^d$ for some $d>0$. Further, the same result holds, with a possibly different $d$, for the choice of $(\sigma_k)$ as in (6), provided $\alpha\ge\beta$.

claims.label: Theorem 3
claims.statement_original:
In the regression model, let us consider the prior on $f$ induced by the heavy-tailed wavelet series prior (4) on coefficients $f_{lk}$ in (16), with parameters specified by (5) and (7)–(8) as well as (14) with $q\ge1$. Suppose $f_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)$ for some $\beta,L>0$. Then, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
E_{f_0}\Pi[\{f:\|f-f_0\|_\infty>\mathcal L_n(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\}\mid X^{(n)}]\to0,
\]
where $\mathcal L_n=(\log n)^d$ for some $d>0$. Further, the same result holds, with a possibly different $d$, for the choice of $(s_l)$ as in (6) and under (14) with any $q\ge1$, provided $\alpha\ge\beta+1/q$.

claims.label: Theorem 4
claims.statement_original:
In the white noise regression model, let $\Pi$ be a heavy tailed prior generated by (4) with parameters specified by (5) and (7)–(8) as well as (14) with $q=2$. Suppose $f_0\in\mathcal B^\beta_{rr}(L)$ for some $\beta,L>0$, $r\in[1,2]$ and $\beta>1/r-1/2$. Then, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
E_{f_0}\Pi[\{f:\|f-f_0\|_2>\mathcal L_nn^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\}\mid X^{(n)}]\to0,
\]
where $\mathcal L_n=(\log n)^d$ for some $d>0$. Further, the same result holds, with a possibly different $d$, for the choice of $(\sigma_k)$ as in (6), provided $\alpha\ge\beta$.

claims.label: Theorem 5
claims.statement_original:
In the regression model, let us consider the heavy-tailed wavelet series prior (4) on coefficients $f_{lk}$ in (16), with parameters specified by (5) and (7)–(8). Consider the multiscale space $\mathcal M_0$ as in (18) with $w_l=l^{1+\kappa+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. Suppose $f_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)$ for some $\beta,L>0$. Then
\[
E_{f_0}\beta_{\mathcal M_0}(\Pi[\cdot\mid X^{(n)}]\circ\tau^{-1},\mathcal L(\mathbb W))\to0
\]
as $n\to\infty$, where $\mathcal L(\mathbb W)$ denotes the law of a Gaussian white noise in $\mathcal M_0$. Further, the same result holds for $(s_l)$ as in (6) with $w_l=l^{(1+\kappa+\varepsilon)/2}$, for some $\varepsilon>0$ (and any $\alpha>0$).

claims.label: Theorem 6 (Generic prior mass condition in $L^2$)
claims.statement_original:
For $\Pi$ a prior generated by (3),

• suppose $(\sigma_k)$ is as in (6) for $\alpha>1/2$ and assume (7)–(8)–(19). For $\beta>0$, let
\[
\varepsilon_n=(\log n)^{\frac{1+(1+\kappa)\beta}{2\beta+1}}n^{-\frac\beta{2\beta+1}}.\tag{20}
\]
Then for any $\beta\le\alpha$, $L>0$ and $f_0\in\mathcal S^\beta(L)$, it holds that for any $d_2>0$ there exists $d_1>0$ sufficiently large such that
\[
\Pi[\|f-f_0\|_2<d_1\varepsilon_n]\ge e^{-d_2n\varepsilon_n^2}.
\]

• suppose $(\sigma_k)$ is defined, for some $a,\delta>0$, by
\[
\sigma_k=e^{-a(\log k)^{1+\delta}},\tag{21}
\]
and assume (7)–(8)–(19). For $\beta>0$, let
\[
\varepsilon_n=(\log n)^{\frac{(1+\kappa)(1+\delta)\beta}{2\beta+1}}n^{-\frac\beta{2\beta+1}}.\tag{22}
\]
Then for any $\beta>0$, $L>0$ and $f_0\in\mathcal S^\beta(L)$, it holds that for any $d_2>0$ there exists $d_1>0$ sufficiently large such that
\[
\Pi[\|f-f_0\|_2<d_1\varepsilon_n]\ge e^{-d_2n\varepsilon_n^2}.
\]

claims.label: Theorem 7 (Generic prior mass condition in $L^\infty$)
claims.statement_original:
For $\Pi$ a prior generated by (4),

• suppose $(s_l)$ is as in (6) for $\alpha>1/2$ and assume (7)–(8)–(19). For $\beta>0$, let
\[
\varepsilon_n=(\log\log n)^{\frac2{1+2\beta}}(\log n)^{\frac{1+(1+\kappa)\beta}{1+2\beta}}n^{-\frac\beta{2\beta+1}}.\tag{23}
\]
Then for any $\beta\le\alpha$, $L>0$ and $f_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)$, it holds that for any $d_2>0$ there exists $d_1>0$ sufficiently large such that, for large enough $n$,
\[
\Pi[\|f-f_0\|_\infty<d_1\varepsilon_n]\ge e^{-d_2n\varepsilon_n^2}.
\]

• suppose $(s_l)$ is as in (5) and assume (7)–(8)–(19). For $\beta>0$, let
\[
\varepsilon_n=(\log n)^{\frac{(2+2\kappa)\beta}{1+2\beta}}n^{-\frac\beta{2\beta+1}}.\tag{24}
\]
Then for any $\beta>0$, $L>0$ and $f_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)$, it holds that for any $d_2>0$ there exists $d_1>0$ sufficiently large such that, for large enough $n$,
\[
\Pi[\|f-f_0\|_\infty<d_1\varepsilon_n]\ge e^{-d_2n\varepsilon_n^2}.
\]

claims.label: Theorem 8 (density estimation)
claims.statement_original:
Consider data $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ sampled independently from a density $g_0$ on $[0,1]$ that is bounded away from 0 and suppose $f_0:=\log g_0\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)$ for some $\beta>0$. Let $\Pi$ be a prior on densities $g$ generated by (25), with parameters on the prior on $f$ as in the statement of Theorem 7 (e.g. $\alpha>1/2$ for the HT($\alpha$) prior) with corresponding rates $\varepsilon_n$ as in (23) or (24). For any $\rho<1$, there exists $M=M(\rho)>0$ with
\[
E_{g_0}\Pi_\rho[\|g-g_0\|_1>M\varepsilon_n\mid X]\to0
\]
as $n\to\infty$, and where $P_0=P_{g_0}$.

claims.label: Theorem 9 (classification)
claims.statement_original:
Consider data $(X,Y)$ from the binary classification model. Suppose $f_0=\Lambda^{-1}h_0$ belongs to the Sobolev ball $\mathcal S^\beta(L)$ for $\beta,L>0$. Let $\Pi$ be a prior generated by (26), with parameters on the prior on $f$ as in the statement of Theorem 6 with corresponding rates $\varepsilon_n$ as in (20) or (22). Then for any given $\rho<1$, there exists $M=M(\rho)$ such that, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
E_{P_0}\Pi_\rho[\|p_f-p_{f_0}\|_{G,1}>M\varepsilon_n\mid X_1,Y_1,\ldots,X_n,Y_n]\to0.
\]

claims.label: Theorem 10
claims.statement_original:
In the white noise regression model, for $\Pi$ a prior generated by (4) and (5), assume (7)–(8)–(19) hold. Suppose $f_0\in\mathcal B^\beta_{rr}(L)$ for some $\beta,L>0$, $r\in[1,2]$ and $\beta>1/r-1/2$. Then, for any given $\rho<1$, as $n\to\infty$,
\[
E_{f_0}\Pi_\rho\left[\{f:\|f-f_0\|_2>\mathcal L_nn^{-\frac\beta{2\beta+1}}\}\mid X^{(n)}\right]\to0,
\]
where $\mathcal L_n=(\log n)^d$ for some $d>0$.

members.local_label: Heavy tailed series priors — constructions (3) and (4)
members.source_heading: Heavy tailed series priors — constructions (3) and (4)
members.statement_original:
Heavy tailed series priors. Depending on the setting, we construct priors in $L^2:=L^2[0,1]$ via series expansions in either an orthonormal basis $\{\varphi_k:k\ge1\}$ or an orthonormal boundary-corrected wavelet basis $\{\psi_{lk}:l\ge0,\ k\in\mathcal K_l\}$ where $\mathcal K_l=\{0,\ldots,2^l-1\}$ and where we denote the scaling function as the first wavelet $\psi_{00}$. Without loss of generality we have taken the coarsest scale to be 1, while it is straightforward to accommodate for coarsest scales finer than 1. For more details, see [40, Section 4.3].

Prior $\Pi$ on functions. For $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ the usual inner product on $L^2$, let $f_k:=\langle f,\varphi_k\rangle$, respectively $f_{lk}:=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$, denote the coefficients of $f\in L^2$ onto the considered bases, so that
\[
f=\sum_{k=1}^\infty f_k\varphi_k,\qquad\text{or}\qquad f=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_l}f_{lk}\psi_{lk}.
\]
Let us define a prior $\Pi$ on $f$ by letting, for $(\sigma_k),(s_l)$ sequences to be chosen below, and $(\zeta_k),(\zeta_{lk})$ independent identically distributed random variables of common law $H$ with heavy tails, also to be specified,
\[
f_k\overset{\mathrm{ind.}}\sim\sigma_k\zeta_k,\tag{3}
\]
in the case of a single–index basis $(\varphi_k)$, or for a double–index basis
\[
f_{lk}\overset{\mathrm{ind.}}\sim s_l\zeta_{lk}.\tag{4}
\]

members.statement_original: Consider a statistical model $\{P_f^{(n)},\ f\in\mathcal F\}$ indexed by a function $f$ with observations $X=X^{(n)}$. Examples considered below include nonparametric regression, density estimation and classification. Given a prior distribution $\Pi$ on $f$, the Bayesian model sets $X\mid f\sim P_f^{(n)}$ and $f\sim\Pi$. The posterior distribution $\Pi[\cdot\mid X]$ is the conditional distribution $f\mid X$. Assuming the model is dominated, the posterior is given as usual by Bayes’ formula. Taking a frequentist approach, we analyse the posterior $\Pi[\cdot\mid X]$ under the assumption that $X$ has actually been generated from $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$ for some fixed true function $f_0$. We refer to the book [38] for more context and references.

members.local_label: Nonparametric regression — Gaussian white noise model (12)
members.source_heading: Nonparametric regression — Gaussian white noise model (12)
members.statement_original:
For $f\in L^2$ and $n\ge1$, the Gaussian white noise model writes
\[
dY^{(n)}(t)=f(t)dt+dW(t)/\sqrt n,\qquad t\in[0,1],\tag{12}
